Sam Altman confirmed that OpenAI is building a humanoid robot

The head of OpenAI directly stated that the company will not only create "brains" for other machines but also its own humanoid.

During the Sources podcast, he was asked if the robots at OpenAI would be human-like or for data centers. The answer was brief: "Both. We will definitely make a humanoid. And other form factors as well."

Altman's logic is simple. The world is already built for humans: doors, keyboards, machines, kitchens. Therefore, at least some of the robots should mimic the human silhouette, otherwise, the entire environment would need to be redesigned.

According to him, the main challenge is not the body but the intelligence that controls this body: "All of this is less important than figuring out how the robot’s brain works."

He doesn't see a household robot as the top priority. First comes infrastructure and production. However, the long-term goal is firm: "Someday, yes. I think everyone should have a personal robot."

This is not yet a product announcement. There's no prototype, pricing, date, or partner factory. But OpenAI is already hiring engineers for actuators, boards, thermal calculations, and firmware — meaning they are assembling hardware, not just software.

The company is entering a field where Tesla, Figure, and others are already working. The difference lies in OpenAI's aspiration to control both the model and the body.

📌 Token Standards: Why Not All Coins Work the Same Way

Main Points
⏺ A token standard defines how a token behaves on a network
⏺ Standards help wallets, exchanges, and dApps understand tokens in the same way
⏺ This post explains why ERC-20, NFTs, and other formats matter in Web3

1️⃣ Core Idea — a standard defines basic token functions: transfers, balances, approvals, and contract interaction.
2️⃣ ERC-20 — the most common format for fungible tokens: every unit is equal to another unit.
3️⃣ NFTs — non-fungible tokens: each item is unique and can represent art, access, items, or rights.
4️⃣ Why It Helps — apps can support new assets faster without custom logic for every project.
5️⃣ Risk Surface — a standard doesn’t prove quality: a scam token can still be technically “valid.”

Final Thoughts

A token standard is a common language for wallets and apps. But the language itself doesn’t tell you whether the project is solid or trash.

🔐 Compliance Data Leak Exposes 291 Crypto Users' Identities

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

⚠️ Bitcoin mining divide pushes Luke Dashjr out of OCEAN 

📣 OCEAN co-founder Luke Dashjr left the Bitcoin mining pool on Aug. 29 after reaching a mutual separation agreement with its parent company, Mummolin Inc. He resigned as chairman, chief technology officer and director. OCEAN and Dashjr attributed the separation to “different visions for the future of Bitcoin mining following the recent protocol developments.” The statement did not identify the developments or explain the areas of disagreement.

📊 The wording therefore does not confirm whether a single Bitcoin protocol proposal caused the split. Dashjr has participated in public debates about transaction policies, mining decentralization and alternative Bitcoin software. Connecting the departure to any particular dispute would require further confirmation from the parties. Dashjr had already stepped back from his OCEAN responsibilities earlier in August. His permanent departure now removes him from the company’s leadership and ownership structure.

🌐 The company did not announce a replacement chairman or chief technology officer. It also provided no details about how Dashjr’s former technical responsibilities will be distributed. Dashjr plans to create a new venture called CONVOY. The joint statement said the project would continue his mission of decentralizing Bitcoin mining.
